findings.message: `md.utils` (set at line 332) is now an ES module namespace object instead of a plain object. Namespace objects are sealed and their properties are read-only, so a plugin that patches or adds to `md.utils` (for example `md.utils.escapeHtml = ...` or `md.utils.myHelper = ...`) now throws a TypeError in strict/ESM code and silently does nothing in sloppy code. The rollup CJS build also freezes the namespace. This is a runtime break of a public API that plugins are encouraged to use. Keep a plain object, e.g. `this.utils = utils.assign({}, utils)` or `{ ...utils }`, the same way `helpers` is copied at line 340.

The `export default` was removed from utils.mjs. package.json exports `./*`, so `markdown-it/lib/common/utils.mjs` is a public deep-import path. Code doing `import utils from 'markdown-it/lib/common/utils.mjs'` will now fail with a SyntaxError (no default export). This breaking change has no deprecation or major version bump. Keep the default export next to the named ones.

`export default { ... }` was changed to named-only exports. Consumers who deep-import `markdown-it/lib/helpers/index.mjs` with a default import, which the public `./*` export map allows, will now get an error. This breaks the public API without notice. Keep a default export as well, or treat this as a semver-major change.
